title: Qu'est-ce qu'un quartier?
oneGoal: Students will understand what a neighborhood is and identify the basic elements that make up their local area
decisionPoints: How familiar are students with their immediate neighborhood?
Should we start with the school area or students' home areas?
What visual aids will help students grasp the concept of neighborhood?
progression: Foundation lesson - introduces the concept of neighborhood as a collection of homes, places, and people
realWorldConnection: Understanding our neighborhood helps us feel safe and connected to our community

title: Ma maison dans mon quartier
oneGoal: Students will locate their home within their neighborhood and understand their place in the local community
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students sharing their address information?
Should we use real addresses or practice with examples?
How do we handle students with temporary or unstable housing?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by helping students identify their specific place within the neighborhood
realWorldConnection: Knowing where we live helps us navigate safely and feel secure in our community

title: Les maisons de mes voisins
oneGoal: Students will explore different types of homes in their neighborhood and understand housing diversity
decisionPoints: How do we discuss housing differences without emphasizing socioeconomic disparities?
Should we focus on architectural features or family living situations?
How do we ensure all housing types are presented positively?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by expanding awareness from own home to neighboring homes and housing variety
realWorldConnection: Different families need different types of homes, and all homes provide safety and belonging

title: Les rues de mon quartier
oneGoal: Students will identify and understand the role of streets in connecting neighborhood places and people
decisionPoints: What level of detail should we include about street safety?
Should we focus on street names or general navigation concepts?
How do we address students who may not walk neighborhood streets regularly?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by examining the pathways that connect homes and create neighborhood structure
realWorldConnection: Streets are like the veins of our neighborhood, connecting all the important places we need

title: Promenade de sécurité dans le quartier
oneGoal: Students will identify safety features and practices for navigating their neighborhood
decisionPoints: What safety concepts are age-appropriate for Grade 1 students?
Should we take an actual neighborhood walk or use virtual exploration?
How do we teach safety without creating fear or anxiety?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by emphasizing safe practices for exploring and moving through neighborhood streets
realWorldConnection: Learning safety rules helps us explore our neighborhood confidently and independently

title: Les commerces près de chez moi
oneGoal: Students will identify local businesses and understand how they serve neighborhood residents
decisionPoints: Which local businesses are most familiar to students?
Should we focus on essential services or include entertainment venues?
How do we represent businesses students may not be able to afford to visit?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by exploring the commercial places that provide goods and services to neighbors
realWorldConnection: Local businesses help meet our daily needs and create jobs for people in our community

title: Qui travaille dans mon quartier?
oneGoal: Students will recognize various workers in their neighborhood and understand how jobs support community life
decisionPoints: Which neighborhood workers are most visible and relatable to students?
Should we include both formal and informal neighborhood workers?
How do we present all types of work as valuable and important?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by examining the people who work in neighborhood businesses and services
realWorldConnection: Many different workers help keep our neighborhood running smoothly and safely

title: Les services publics de mon quartier
oneGoal: Students will identify public services in their neighborhood and understand how they benefit everyone
decisionPoints: Which public services are most accessible and familiar to students?
Should we focus on recreational services or essential services first?
How do we explain the concept of 'public' to Grade 1 students?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by exploring community services that are available to all neighborhood residents
realWorldConnection: Public services belong to everyone in our community and help make our neighborhood better

title: Ma carte du quartier
oneGoal: Students will create a simple map of their neighborhood showing important places and landmarks
decisionPoints: What mapping skills are developmentally appropriate for Grade 1?
Should maps be drawn from memory or with visual references?
How do we help students understand spatial relationships and scale?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by synthesizing neighborhood knowledge into a visual representation
realWorldConnection: Making maps helps us understand where things are and plan our routes through the neighborhood

title: Exploration guidée du quartier
oneGoal: Students will take a guided walk through their neighborhood to observe and identify key features
decisionPoints: What route would be safest and most educational for a class walk?
Should parents/volunteers be involved in the neighborhood exploration?
How do we ensure all students can participate in physical exploration?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by providing direct, experiential learning about neighborhood features
realWorldConnection: Walking through our neighborhood helps us notice details and feel more connected to our community

title: Les changements dans mon quartier
oneGoal: Students will observe how neighborhoods change over time and identify current changes in their area
decisionPoints: How do we discuss neighborhood changes without emphasizing gentrification or displacement?
Should we focus on physical changes or community changes?
How do we help students see change as both normal and sometimes challenging?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by introducing the concept that neighborhoods evolve and change over time
realWorldConnection: Neighborhoods change as families grow, businesses develop, and communities evolve

title: Comment prendre soin de mon quartier
oneGoal: Students will identify ways they can help keep their neighborhood clean, safe, and beautiful
decisionPoints: What neighborhood care activities are age-appropriate for Grade 1 students?
Should we focus on individual actions or community cooperation?
How do we encourage environmental stewardship without overwhelming students?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by empowering students to take positive action in their neighborhood
realWorldConnection: Taking care of our neighborhood helps everyone feel proud and happy to live there

title: Les transports dans mon quartier
oneGoal: Students will identify different ways people move around their neighborhood and understand transportation options
decisionPoints: Which transportation methods are most common in students' neighborhood?
Should we focus on public transit, private vehicles, or active transportation?
How do we discuss transportation equity and accessibility?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by exploring how people and goods move through neighborhood spaces
realWorldConnection: Different types of transportation help people get to work, school, and the places they need to go

title: Les espaces verts de mon quartier
oneGoal: Students will identify parks, gardens, and green spaces in their neighborhood and understand their importance
decisionPoints: What green spaces are accessible to students in their neighborhood?
Should we focus on formal parks or include all natural areas?
How do we discuss environmental benefits at an age-appropriate level?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by highlighting the natural and recreational spaces within the neighborhood
realWorldConnection: Green spaces give us places to play, relax, and connect with nature in our neighborhood

title: Rencontrer des voisins
oneGoal: Students will understand how to be good neighbors and appreciate the people who live nearby
decisionPoints: How do we encourage social connection while teaching appropriate stranger safety?
Should we invite community members to visit the classroom?
How do we represent the diversity of neighborhood residents positively?
progression: Builds on Lesson 14 by focusing on the social connections that make neighborhoods feel like communities
realWorldConnection: Getting to know our neighbors helps create a friendly, caring community where everyone feels welcome

title: Les événements du quartier
oneGoal: Students will learn about community events and celebrations that bring neighbors together
decisionPoints: What community events are appropriate and accessible for young families?
Should we focus on regular events or special celebrations?
How do we include diverse cultural celebrations that happen in the neighborhood?
progression: Builds on Lesson 15 by exploring how neighborhoods celebrate and gather as communities
realWorldConnection: Community events help neighbors get to know each other and celebrate what makes our area special

title: Problèmes et solutions du quartier
oneGoal: Students will identify simple neighborhood challenges and brainstorm age-appropriate solutions
decisionPoints: What neighborhood problems are appropriate to discuss with Grade 1 students?
Should we focus on environmental issues or social challenges?
How do we maintain optimism while acknowledging real community concerns?
progression: Builds on Lesson 16 by introducing critical thinking about community improvement
realWorldConnection: When neighbors work together, they can solve problems and make their community even better

title: Projet d'amélioration du quartier
oneGoal: Students will plan a simple project to improve their neighborhood and understand their role as active citizens
decisionPoints: What improvement project is realistic and achievable for Grade 1 students?
Should the project focus on environmental action or community connection?
How do we ensure the project feels meaningful without being overwhelming?
progression: Builds on Lesson 17 by taking action to address neighborhood needs through student initiative
realWorldConnection: Even young people can make a positive difference in their neighborhood through caring actions

title: Présenter mon quartier
oneGoal: Students will create a presentation about their neighborhood to share with others
decisionPoints: What format would work best for student neighborhood presentations?
Should presentations focus on facts or personal experiences?
How do we help students feel proud of their neighborhood regardless of its challenges?
progression: Builds on Lesson 18 by synthesizing learning into a celebration of neighborhood knowledge and pride
realWorldConnection: Sharing what we know about our neighborhood helps others understand and appreciate our community

title: Je suis fier de mon quartier
oneGoal: Students will reflect on their neighborhood learning and express pride in their local community
decisionPoints: How do we help students articulate what they've learned about neighborhoods?
Should reflection focus on personal connection or community understanding?
How do we end the unit with genuine pride regardless of neighborhood challenges?
progression: Culminating lesson that celebrates student growth in neighborhood awareness and community connection
realWorldConnection: Feeling proud of where we live helps us care for our community and work to make it even better
